analysis:
This batch contains documentation-only changes. The inference.md units 7-9 (head 406-1203) are unchanged surrounding text. The actual changes are the date line and head 252-259, which fall in another unit; the file_changes patch shows they add a note that SSD staging runs before engine.submit. The same patch says a provider-staged complete-checkpoint import creates destinations from host bytes without evaluating or fencing them, so it never waits on MLX-Swift's evalLock. prefix-cache.md head 784-790 adds the same statement and says the import plan charges the largest host-zero source as staging scratch. No source code is changed in this batch.

Relevant to T-041(e), the no-persistent-memory-carve posture: transient staging RAM is charged to GlobalKVCacheBudget per staged entry. The docs claim the host-zero scratch is charged. Integration should verify against CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift that two things hold. First, scratch accounting stays within the shared staging reservation. Second, skipping eval/fence on destinations created from host bytes cannot let an engine read uninitialized or partially written KV. A wrong state would be a correctness or confidentiality issue; it is relevant to T-028 residual GPU memory and to cross-request data.

Also confirm that the DBK3 AES-GCM authentication (T-041(c)) still completes before any destination becomes available to the engine. The phrase "already available from host bytes" implies the decrypted, authenticated payload is copied first. That ordering is not verifiable from the docs alone.

No threat-model gap is evident. The changes do not alter TTL, the HMAC naming of on-disk files, salt scoping or the kill switch. If the source code is in another batch, check its staging-reservation release paths (SSDPrefixCache.endAdoption/completeStaging) per the T-041 detection_hint.
